Fulham manager Marco Silva promised a decision next week on his future and admitted his team missed the “cherry on the cake” by failing to qualify for Europe.

A 2-0 win over Newcastle at Craven Cottage will have been a fitting send-off if, as looks likely, the lure of replacing Jose Mourinho at Benfica proves sufficiently tempting for Silva to walk away after five years in charge.

Fulham have offered a three-year deal for him to stay but as supporters said goodbye for the summer to their team in west London, there was a sense that one farewell might have been for good.

“In this moment, I’m being honest with you, I don’t feel like that, because I haven’t decided,” said Silva. “If I have made my decision, I don’t have any problem to say.

“If I haven’t announced anything and the club haven’t announced anything, it’s because I haven’t decided. It’s not going to be longer than next week. It cannot happen.

“I don’t like to play games. In this moment I haven’t made my decision. It’s going to be next week for sure. We have to announce because the club has to move on, or for me to be here we have many things to prepare.”

Fulham fell a win short of a memorable season despite comfortably dispatching a toothless Newcastle side.

Three more points would have propelled them to a Europa League place and when the final standings are looked at, the 1-0 defeat to sixth-place Bournemouth here on 9 May will be the game that stands out as the moment Fulham’s fate ran away from them.

There was at least a wonderful goal from Tom Cairney, flashed into the top corner from 25 yards in the second half, to send supporters away happy – even if that feeling only lasts until Silva reveals his decision in a few days.

Issa Diop had earlier headed Fulham in front, reacting quickest to nod home after Kevin’s glorious arching free-kick had struck the bar.

It was not enough. Fulham finished 11th, a single point off qualifying for the Conference League.

“We missed the cherry on the cake,” said Silva. “I’m the first one to say.”

Newcastle’s season has been more starkly disappointing. A run of one win in seven in January and February effectively ended their Champions League hopes, and four losses in a row that came later led to a dispiriting finish of 12th.

“Not the way we want to end the season, that’s for sure,” said boss Eddie Howe, who has been told his job is safe despite a poor campaign.

“There was a disjointed view about the team, in part because we had limited selection choices. We didn’t like how we performed. Really frustrating.

“It’s been a really difficult season. The number of games we played, the focus going from Europe back to the Premier League is always a challenge. We haven’t dealt with that well enough in our Premier League season.

“The squad had a disjointed look to it towards the end of the season with injuries and lots of other stuff. It’s been a tough and challenging campaign but one the team will come through stronger for.”

A friend of Stewart McLean has spoken out after the Virgin River actor was found dead in British Columbia.

The remains of McLean, 45, were found by Canada’s Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT) on Friday, May 22. His death is being investigated as a homicide.

Speaking to The Canadian Press, McLean’s friend and acting coach Jeff Seymour said he knew something was very wrong as soon as the actor failed to turn up for filming last Saturday.

"He was meticulous about everything, and there would be no chance he blew it off or slept too late. As soon as I heard he didn't make it on Saturday morning, I knew there was big trouble," said Seymour.

Seymour went on to describe McLean as a “straight arrow” and added, “It just doesn't make any sense. He was incredibly situationally aware. I bring it up because for the life of me, I don't know how anybody could get the drop on him.”

'Virgin River' actor Stewart McLean was reported missing on on May 18 ( RCMP )

Seymour, who is based in Los Angeles, said he became “fast friends” with McLean after he attended one of his coaching sessions eight years ago.

"Everybody loved this guy, it wasn't like he was in nefarious activities or, you know, kind of ran with another crowd,” continued Seymour. “I mean, he was a bit of a loner. He spent a lot of time reading and being at his home out there in Squamish.”

He added: “It's just a shocker. I would love to see justice served.”

McLean’s remains were found in the Lions Bay area of British Columbia, according to police. The Edmonton-born actor was last seen at his home in Lions Bay, British Columbia, according to reports. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) in Squamish subsequently received a missing person report on May 18. RCMP turned the case over to IHIT on May 20.

In a statement to The Independent, Cpl. Esther Tupper of IHIT said: “As the investigation continues to unfold, homicide investigators are working to collect and analyze evidence, review CCTV footage and conduct interviews to build a timeline of Mr. McLean’s activities prior to May 15, 2026. We are pursuing all available leads as we work to find answers for the family, friends and loved ones of Mr. McLean.”

Police have encouraged anyone with any information regarding McLean’s death to call the IHIT information line at 1-877-551-IHIT (4448) or by email at ihitinfo@rcmp–grc.gc.ca.

The actor, who has often been credited as Stew McLean, worked in the entertainment industry for over a decade. His earliest credits include an appearance in the 2016 television film Signed, Sealed, Delivered: One in a Million, the DC superhero show Arrow and the fantasy series Supernatural.

McLean’s more recent credits include an episode of the Canadian series Murder in a Small Town and the crime drama Happy Face.

He also regularly appeared in short films and worked as a producer, and often filmed near Vancouver, including on Bowen Island and in Squamish.

Departing Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola thought it was “almost impossible” to take the club into Europe this season after his side secured sixth place with a 1-1 draw against Nottingham Forest.

Morgan Gibbs-White gave the home side a first-half lead with a free-kick – his 18th goal in all competitions this term.

Bournemouth got themselves level nine minutes after the break courtesy of Marcus Tavernier’s strike but it was not enough for the Cherries to secure a Champions League place.

They will, however, play in the Europa League for the first time in the club’s history.

Iraola, who announced in April that he would be leaving, helped Bournemouth finish the campaign on an 18-match unbeaten run and the 43-year-old could not stop smiling in his post-match press conference.

He admitted he did not want the run to end in his final game, and said: “I feel so happy because I could not ask for much more.

“I didn’t want to lose today, I wanted to finish sixth. Also I wanted to finish the season without losing so we can do the second half of the season unbeaten. This is the most difficult achievement we’ve got.

“I enjoyed every second with the fans, with the players. It’s nice to finish like this, something to celebrate. Honestly happy and in the changing room we were celebrating like we should.

“I knew it would be almost impossible to get Europe but the owner told me we want to stay in the Premier League, but I wanted Europe.

“For me to finish this season giving back to the owner, players, supporters, this European qualification is just one way of thanking everyone.”

The Forest fans even stayed behind to applaud Iraola and his team off.

The Spaniard added: “Class from the Forest fans. Forest have done it last season, in semi-finals. They recognise what we have done.”

Gibbs-White missed out on a place in England’s World Cup squad this week and responded by celebrating a goal which seemingly sent a message to Thomas Tuchel – pointing to his chest and raising 10 fingers.

Reds boss Vitor Pereira felt the attacking midfielder had done everything he could to compete in the summer tournament.

He said: “We had a conversation. We can’t do everything. We should do everything to get our targets and try to compete, the results we cannot control.

“He did everything to deserve to be in the national team but in the end it is not his decision. He is disappointed of course because he score goals, assists, he’s a leader, talent and real connector. In the end he’s in a country with a lot of strong players.”

Pereira was Forest’s fourth manager of the season and he feels the club needs “stability” to kick on next season.

He added: “In my opinion we created a true spirit. Now we have a good environment, we feel confidence in each other.

“I believe if we want to compete for different goals, we need to keep the best players. If not, it will be difficult to be consistent and build something stronger.”

News.title: Emma Raducanu’s French Open over after error-strewn first-round defeat
News.content:
Emma Raducanu suffered her first opening-round exit at the French Open after being bageled in the first set in a match more memorable for errors than winners.

After a 6-0 opening set over in just 25 minutes, the match looked like it would hardly cause Solana Sierra to break a sweat, but Raducanu fought back in the second set, though it was not enough to force a decider.

The British No 1 looked every bit as rusty as might be expected, considering she arrived at Roland Garros having only played one tour match since March 8. But even taking that into consideration, the first set was still far below the level expected of a player who has only just dropped out of the seeded positions.

Raducanu made 15 unforced errors while delivering no winners as she was unable to win a game in a set that hardly lasted long enough for fans to take their seats, while Sierra made a blistering start. In fact, Raducanu only won 11 points in the first set, despite Sierra only hitting 35 per cent of her first serves.

News.title: Tottenham hold their nerve to survive on a day of agony
News.content:
De Zerbi, who arrived in a crisis, and is new to all this, has now built a bond with the fans the like of which his predecessors Frank, and Tudor, never enjoyed. That will be crucial in setting Spurs’ sights a little higher. De Zerbi was in a playful mood afterwards, demanding in his press conference the presence of a journalist he considered to be “negative” but only “to give him a hug”. “From tonight we have to organise and to build the new team,” De Zerbi said, before adding that it would not be a complete clear-out. “I think we have not to change too many players. We have 10, 11, 12 players good enough to stay.”

That would have focused a few minds in the home dressing room. As for Everton, this was the finale to a season-ending slump that has removed all hope of European qualification. When they beat Chelsea at home on March 31, David Moyes’s team were eighth. Since then they have not won one of the final seven matches of the season – from which they have taken three points. It has been a stagger to 13th place although, as West Ham have demonstrated, life post-Moyes can be much worse.

“I’m absolutely p----d [off] with it,” Moyes said later, “you wouldn’t expect me to be any other way.” He will discover this summer just what ambition the Friedkin Group have for Everton in the long term. He acknowledged that his team had not played well in the first half and yet in spite of that they had not let Spurs put the game out of reach.

Palhinha’s goal was an unusual one – a header against a post which he then pushed over the line with his left foot when the ball came back to him. De Zerbi has preferred that grinding midfield trio of Palhinha, Bentancur and Gallagher over the youthful Lucas Bergvall and Archie Gray, who did make a substitute appearance late on in the game. On this occasion it came through for him. Spurs mustered two attempts on target all game. Van de Ven got his foot to a cross from George before the substitute had Everton’s one attempt on target, to which Kinsky was the equal.

News.title: Russell takes last-gasp pole after clashing with Antonelli in Canada sprint
News.content:
Antonelli was told to calm down by race engineer Peter “Bono” Bonnington after his outburst over the radio after the first incident. But when he carried on complaining, he earned a rebuke from his team principal Toto Wolff, who told him to “concentrate on the driving”.

Then, at the end of the race, after Antonelli went off track a third time trying to pass Norris and was looking to vent his spleen again on the cool-down lap, Wolff shut him down a second time. “Kimi, now is not the time to talk about this. We will talk about this later, not on the radio.”

The two Mercedes men had a brief handshake after getting out of their cars, but it promised to be an awkward debrief.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Martin Brundle said it was no surprise to see the two come to blows given they are fighting for the title. Russell is under pressure this weekend because Antonelli has won the last three races to take the championship lead.

“It was always going to happen. Inevitable. Kimi lost his head a little bit but he’ll learn from this,” was Brundle’s verdict.

The fighting at the front was the highlight of an entertaining sprint race in general. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton looked as if he would take fourth spot for most of the race, only to clip the “Wall of Champions” late in the race. Hamilton was then passed by McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, losing position, which allowed Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc to pass him as well.

News.title: Oli McBurnie spies £200m tap-in to fire unlikely lads Hull to Premier League
News.content:
This is a manager and squad that have fostered an admirable team spirit, although they now find themselves in late May staring up at a challenge on a completely different scale to that which came before. At the very least one could say that they have acclimatised to playing without the ball. Jakirovic also looks like a quick learner – epitomised by his record against Middlesbrough this season. Hull were 4-0 down to Boro at home in early December and eventually lost 4-1, but won at the Riverside Stadium at the end of the month.

The Boro manager Kim Hellberg acknowledged that his players had not been “sharp enough” to create the chances their domination of the ball might have warranted. Their year has taken some turns. The manager they sacked one year ago is now in charge of Manchester United on a two-year contract. Michael Carrick’s successor Rob Edwards is back in the Championship with Wolverhampton Wanderers. Boro’s best player, Hayden Hackney, will now assume – for the second time this month – that he has played his last game for the club.

Hackney, 23, the hometown hero, came off the bench in the second half having not played since March 14 with a calf injury. Having watched the play-off semi-final defeat to Southampton he will have thought that was the end. It certainly is now with Premier League clubs circling, and Crystal Palace thought to be the likely destination. There were fine performances from the US international Aidan Morris in midfield and Luke Ayling at centre-back, and both had plenty of the ball. They just found it impossible to create a chance.

Both teams would have required major changes to be competitive in the Premier League and for Hull, back from the brink of League One, it is a giant step up. They can enjoy their day of triumph but the next 38 league games will be the test of their lives.

News.title: How to have a happy dog and other tips from vets, breeders and trainers
News.content:
Perhaps your dog is easily agitated and you’ve never been able to understand why. According to Dr Wedderburn, the answer might be – and don’t laugh – childhood trauma. “Many, many dogs these days are reactive and get anxious in new situations,” he explains. “They get aggressive and fearful, which is often because they’re badly socialised when they’re young.”

“Puppies have a socialisation window in their brain up until four months of age,” Dr Wedderburn says. “Whenever they come across a new experience, their brain will accept it as being part of the normal world. If they don’t meet experiences until they’re older than that, until they’re maybe five or six months of age, then their brain is fearful and anxious instead and they retain that fear and anxiety for the rest of their lives.”

Trainer Cox has plenty of experience dealing with anxious dogs: “The most important thing is to recognise that the dog is overstimulated and remove them from that environment. Some dogs like gentle stroking, others like a quiet, calm voice or soft food or something else to chew. Maybe a snuffle mat that they can do a little bit of sniffy work – that tends to take their arousal levels down.”

Why are vet fees so expensive?

News.title: Leinster humiliated as ruthless Bordeaux retain Champions Cup crown
News.content:
This time there was no Champions Cup final heartbreak for Leinster, just humiliation. In their previous four defeats at the final reckoning, the Irish province could look agonisingly to key moments when the pursuit of a fifth star fell just short.

But this was different. This time there could be no gnashing of teeth, no looking back ruefully at squandered opportunities. This time they came up alarmingly short against a Bordeaux-Bègles side who have, in the eight years since Leinster won the last of their Champions Cup crowns, established themselves as the new European superpower.

The manner in which they retained their title was, quite simply stunning, with all the damage done in a first half that yielded five converted tries, finished by their outstanding captain, Maxime Lucu, Pablo Uberti, Louis Bielle-Biarrey (2) and Yoram Moefana.

They have not lost a Champions Cup game since being beaten by Harlequins in the quarter-finals during the 2023-24 season. The arrival of Tom Willis from Saracens will only strengthen their hand.

News.title: Uganda confirms three more Ebola cases
News.content:
Uganda has confirmed three more Ebola cases as the burgeoning outbreak from neighbouring Congo continues to spread.

Health officials said the new cases brought the total detected in Uganda to five.

Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains the epicentre of the outbreak but the World Health Organization warned there was a high risk of the infection spreading to other east African countries.

A week after the outbreak was first confirmed, DRC authorities reported that the flare-up was already the third largest on record, with 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.

Relief efforts are being hampered by insecurity in Ituri and the fact the outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, rather than the Zaire strain, which caused 15 of the DRC’s previous 17 outbreaks. There are no approved vaccines for the variant, which can kill up to half of those it infects.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick speaks out on Bruno Fernandes’ Manchester United future after assists record
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK has no doubt that Bruno Fernandes will stay at Manchester United next season.

Fernandes set the Premier League record for assists in a single campaign by crossing for Patrick Dorgu’s opening goal in United’s 3-0 rout of Brighton.





The United captain has claimed the Football Writers’ Association Player of the Year award, the Premier League Player of the Season and the Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year award in recent weeks.

United were prepared to cash in on Fernandes last summer amid an £80million offer from Saudi club Al Nassr.

Fernandes has a £57m release clause in his contract that can be triggered by an overseas club but United have taken measures to ensure that he remains beyond the summer.

When asked about Fernandes’ future, Carrick said: “He’s such an influence for us and he’s been the captain and led by example in different ways.



“So, yeah, I’ve got no reason to think otherwise. We’ve loved what he’s done, and he loves being here.

“I think you can see that. He wanted to stay on, he wants to stay on every single game, because he’s enjoying his football, which is fantastic.”

Fernandes also scored as United ended their season on a high with a first double over Brighton since the 2020-21 season.

The scoreline marked Carrick’s biggest win in charge in what was his first match since United appointed him in a permanent capacity on Friday.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

That story was overshadowed by Pep Guardiola’s departure from Manchester City and the England World Cup squad announcement, which helped to ensure United’s preparations felt natural.

“I half forgot that it was the first game since I’ve been announced, really,” Carrick admitted. “We were just carrying on as normal.

“We’ve treated it as all one season going into the next one, really. It’s not ended here.

“I think we wanted to keep building and keep pushing. Credit to the players.



“It’s not easy to do that, sometimes, to do it as much as we’d expected.

“And I’ve been there, and it’s hard to find that spark. But the hunger was there, you could see it.

“And it was probably the toughest team to play that type of game in the heat, the way they move the ball.

“So it needed a really strong mentality. which I was absolutely delighted with, because that’s the foundation we need to show and have, to give us the confidence to move forward.”



Fernandes eclipsed Thierry Henry and Kevin de Bruyne with his assists record and thanked his team-mates for their conversion rate.

“It was already special being in their company,” Fernandes said of Henry and De Bruyne. “We are talking about two players that made the Premier League so great, and they were two of the greatest in the Premier League.

“My style of playing has always been the same. Creation has not been something that has changed or improved.

“The biggest difference is my team-mates have scored more goals than before, and I get the credit for that.”

Sports.title: Man City fans fume at Micah Richards after finding out why he missed Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY fans were not happy with Micah Richards after he was deployed at Selhurst Park for the final day of the season.

Richards, who played 245 games for the club, retains an ambassador role for the Cityzens alongside his punditry work.





However, the former full-back was not present at the Etihad Stadium for the final game of Bernardo Silva, John Stones and, especially, Pep Guardiola.

The 37-year-old was instead at Selhurst Park for Arsenal lifting the Premier League trophy after a 22-year wait.

Of course, he might have precious little say over where he is enlisted on game days.

But social media certainly didn’t take that into account!

One user wrote: “Micah Richards is our club Ambassador. He’s at Arsenal’s game and not at City’s. Telling since ages to remove this guy. And you are’nt doing. Passionate supporters of the club like Joe Hart are not given any chance.”

Another posted: “Still amazes me that Richards is a city ambassador considering the amount of cheering on publicly he has done for Arsenal. Taking the p***, and I like him.”

A third commented: “Our Club Ambassador, Micah Richards, is at the Arsenal game not Pep’s final game. What a disgrace.”

A fourth tweeted: “City need to jib Micah Richards on.”

The 37-year-old did praise Guardiola during the Sky Sports broadcast which also featured Ian Wright and Jamie Redknapp.

He said: “Leader, legend, trend-setter… he;s the best of his generation without a doubt and he’s arguably the best to ever grace football.

“Just because of the way he played the game. And he was questioned about the way he wanted to play, could he come here and do tippy-tappy football? He absolutely conquered it.”

Sports.title: ‘Blows my mind’ – Gary Neville goes on major rant as Tottenham vs Everton bizarrely halted before Spurs dodge relegation
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE went on a major rant as Tottenham’s game was halted in bizarre fashion.

And that meant their crunch second half did not start at the same time as West Ham’s.





Tottenham beat Everton 1-0 to cling on to their Premier League status.

That sent West Ham down, even though the Hammers beat Leeds 3-0.

However, there was controversy at the start of the second half.

Tottenham and West Ham were both supposed to begin the second half simultaneously so they were synced up for the integrity of the relegation battle.



But the referees suffered a technical problem with their communication devices.

That meant the action at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium got underway five minutes later than at the London Stadium.

So when the full-time whistle sounded in East London, the match in North London was only just going into a minimum of nine added minutes – although it ended up being an extra 11.

And Sky Sports commentator Neville was livid at the tech blunder.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He blasted: “Honestly… what blows my mind is that they have had nearly 20 minutes to check it.

“Why have they kicked off there if they’re synchronising it?

“I don’t think a football match should be stopped for this.

“This is not good enough, I get you have technical problems.

“The fans are booing, and rightly so.



“I’m furious with this, not just because it’s the last game of the season, sporting integrity.

“There’s an element of always kicking off together when you’re fighting for something.

“It’s absolutely ridiculous, it’s a warm day today, but it could be winter and -2 with players walking around. It’s not good enough.”

In the end, it mattered little because West Ham secured their win but Tottenham were leading anyway.

And the delay meant Hammers players and staff had a long, painful wait on the pitch for their fate to be confirmed.

Sports.title: Man City 1 Aston Villa 2: Pep Guardiola’s decade of decadence ends in loss as Ollie Watkins fires out World Cup warning
Sports.content:
OLLIE WATKINS sent Pep Guardiola to a losing send-off as his decade of Manchester City glory ended in a defeat that did not really matter.

On the day that the Etihad rose as one to say farewell to arguably the greatest manager of the Premier League era, Guardiola suffered a rare home upset.





It looked as though the Catalan’s penultimate signing was going to mark the occasion with a final victory goal.

Antoine Semenyo’s lovely back post volley, eight days after the exquisite flick that completed the domestic cup double, was his 21st of the season and 11th since his January move from Bournemouth.

But two minutes into the second half, Watkins took full advantage of a back post blunder from John Stones – not the way the England defender wanted his sign-off to go – to squeeze home the leveller.

And just after the hour, he danced away down the right for a second – after a long VAR check overturned the original flag – with Stones left flat on his back.

It would have represented mixed news for Thomas Tuchel, especially as he has earmarked Stones for a World Cup starting role.

With the City fans really waiting for the final whistle to allow them to say goodbye to the club’s finest boss, this was one time when it was less about the game than the occasion, tears for souvenirs in all directions.

Even so, while City wanted to give the Spanish gaffer his perfect send-off – Phil Foden, perhaps, with a point to prove, was denied a last-gasp leveller by VAR – Villa initially appeared exhausted, the remnants of a team still celebrating Wednesday night in Istanbul.

No blame there.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Evenings like that only come along every 44 years or so.

The surprise was that it took 23 minutes for the home side’s pressure to count.

Tijjani Reijnders and Bernardo Silva had already both gone close before the Dutch midfielder’s inswinging corner from the left-ing was inadvertently flicked on by Lamare Bogarde for Semenyo to cushion a volley back past Marco Bizot and into the far corner.

It was the 1423rd goal under the Catalan, on the day that he broke Les McDowell’s record of 592 games in the City hotseat.



Guardiola barely twitched although he was on the edge of his technical area to witness Savinho rolling a couple of inches wide and Reijnders firing a free-kick fractionally over the top before he was denied by an excellent Bizot stop just before the break.

Yet Villa equalised barely a minute after the interval, from their first attempt on goal.

Again it came from a corner mistake, Stones, like Silva and the manager making his final appearance, heading a clearance straight at Watkins, who pounced from close range.



A weeping Silva left to a guard of honour from both sets of players, while Guardiola had given Gianluigi Donnarumma, Rodri and Erling Haaland the afternoon off.

And soon afterwards, Watkins had his second, escaping down the right from Ross Barkley’s pass, leaving Stones on his backside before poking past James Trafford.

The flag went up but the first replay told a different story, Ruben Dias playing him onside, as Stockley Park eventually confirmed.



Stones, too, received a standing ovation and guard of honour when he was replaced, seconds after Leon Bailey had smashed against the bar for resurgent Villa.

Chances at both ends followed, Jeremy Doku a whisker wide, Trafford denying John McGinn’s curler.

When Foden, fed by Mateo Kovacic, crashed in off the bar in the final minute, it looked as if he had rescued a point.



Once again, Stockley Park, rightly, intervened – although the Etihad giant screens showed a graphic that appeared to put Foden ONSIDE.

You can guess how they went down.

Yet the scoreline did not prevent the Guardiola chants ringing round once more.

They all know things will never be the same again.

Sports.title: Sunderland 2 Chelsea 1: Dire Blues season ends with NO Euro football but Black Cats in seventh heaven with Europa League
Sports.content:
NETFLIX missed a trick by not recording this heroic season for their “Sunderland ‘Til I Die” docuseries.

They missed another by not making a horror about the “World Champions” nightmare campaign.





Sunderland’s domination of the billion-pound Blues, to qualify for European football for the first time 1973, would have been the perfect season finale to an underdog story for the ages.

Steel, passion, and determination. They had it all on the final day.



Little more than the opposite can be said for Chelsea’s overpaid and under-working stars who were outrun and outplayed once more.

The smell of smoke filled the nostrils of anyone within a five-mile radius of the Stadium of Light as far as two hours ahead of kick-off, with Sunderland fans desperate to roar their team into a European spot next season.

Red flares were carried by children as young as 12 and pensioners in the North East of England, as they sang songs about their heroic Swiss midfielder, Granit Xhaka.

The arrival of the home team bus gave competition to the warm welcomes received by champions Arsenal and Spurs in their bid for Premier League survival.



Inside the ground, a cauldron of red and white shirts piled the pressure on to the Blues, who were looking to salvage some European football of their own from a disaster season.

Three points against Spurs on Tuesday with a rotated side meant that Calum McFarlane’s side, to be inherited by Xabi Alonso on the 1st of June, could end up in the Europa League, Conference League, or with no European football at all next season.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The first chance fell to Cole Palmer, fresh from his lack of World Cup selection disappoint.

Thomas Tuchel’s disparaging comments about his form rang true again, as he got in behind the Sunderland defence only to produce a tame effort that fell at the feet of Robin Roefs.



Truth be told, it was the hosts who looked more likely to score in the opening 20 minutes.

Sunderland became artists, painting delicate pass maps out from the back before Enzo Le Fee bolted down the right and lashed a shot into the gloves of Robert Sanchez.

Other chances fell to Nordi Mukiele and Nilsson Angulo from range, with Brian Brobbey almost capitalising on a lack of communication inside the Chelsea penalty box.

Sunderland fans cheered every attempt so loudly you’d be forgiven for thinking that no Chelsea fans had bothered to even make the journey.

They were dominant on and off the pitch, and made it count with 25 minutes gone.



A long ball over the top saw Jorrel Hato climb over his marker, but poor contact on the header saw the ball land on the outside of Trai Hume’s right foot.

Hume did what Palmer couldn’t, and dispatched the ball into the corner with just enough power to beat Sanchez in net.

It felt apt that Hume and O’Nien, both who had come up with Sunderland from League One, combined for the opener.

And good news soon became great news.

At 1-0 up, news travelled quickly from the south to the north that Bruno Fernandes had broken the Premier League assist record and put Man Utd a goal to the good.



A goal that saw Sunderland into a Europa League place at the expense of their opponents.

Joao Pedro should’ve levelled the scoring before half-time, but Malo Gusto’s teasing cross went to waste when the Brazilian headed wide.

The half-time whistle bought an opportunity for the Chelsea players to check their phones and see that a point would be enough to reach the Europa League if other results stayed the same.



But it didn’t seem to bring them much encouragement, as Brobbey missed a huge chance to double Sunderland’s lead, powering through on goal before being denied by Sanchez.

Three minutes later, the Black Cats pounced again.

Le Fee cut the ball back for Brobbey, whose wayward effort was turned home by Gusto to make it 2-0.

Sunderland fans’ excitement spilled over and supporters were almost on the pitch when an advertising hoarding collapsed amid the celebrations.

The Blues looked a team determined NOT to play in Europe next season, aside from Palmer, who got them back in it.



The 24-year-old looked like he had a point to prove to Tuchel, with plenty of shots and one that eventually got the better of Robin Roefs after 56 minutes, though even that lacked a bit of conviction.

Wilson Isidor’s ingenious flick over Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana saw the latter given his marching orders with half an hour to play when he dragged his countryman to the deck.

It was another sign of the ill-discipline that has plagued Chelsea this season, and a warning sign to the incoming Alonso who will need to deal with that.

At least the Spaniard will have plenty of time in bleak, quiet midweeks next season to deal with it.

Sports.title: Arsenal fans love new Premier League rule introduced for final day of season as they make most of it at Crystal Palace

ARSENAL fans were loving a rule introduced for the final day of the Premier League season.

The Gunners were out parading their title win with a visit to Selhurst Park in south London.

But with the extreme heat, Prem chiefs introduced a water break rule in the middle of the halves.

And Arsenal fans, watching their team for the first time since becoming champions and banishing their “bottlers tag”, didn’t pass up the chance to hit back at the trolls who had branded them as such earlier this season.

Sports.title: West Ham RELEGATED from Premier League after 14 years despite final day heroics as nervy Spurs just about cling on
Sports.content:
WEST HAM have been RELEGATED from the Premier League after 14 years in the top flight – as Tottenham clung on to survival on the final day of the season.

A disastrous season means that the Hammers will host Championship football at the 62,500-seater London Stadium next term.





The East Londoners won the Conference League in 2023 and contested a Europa League quarter-final barely two years ago.

But they went into the Prem finale needing to beat Leeds at home… and for Everton to win away at Tottenham.



And it proved too much of an ask.

The Hammers did all they could as Taty Castellanos headed in from a corner midway through the second half to break the deadlock.

Jarrod Bowen raced clear with ten minutes left and slotted home for 2-0 before Callum Wilson added a third deep into injury time.

But across town, Joao Palhinha had already given Spurs the lead just before half-time when his rebound just crossed the line.



That left the Hammers needing two big helping hands from Everton.

But neither were forthcoming as Spurs held on for a 1-0 win after 11 added minutes – so Tottenham avoided the drop at West Ham’s painful expense.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Here’s how SunSport reporter Jack Rosser summed up what went wrong at the London Stadium this season…

From Conference League to Championship, West Ham’s chronic mismanagement has turned opportunity into embarrassment.

Ten years after a world-class team in a world-class stadium was promised upon their move to the London Stadium, the Hammers have finally been relegated.

It is somewhat of a miracle they still had a shot at survival on the last day, but the issues stretch back longer than just this season.

Three years ago, the club were celebrating their first major trophy in 43 years.



Since then, West Ham have dispensed of the manager who delivered not only that trophy but three straight years in Europe, David Moyes, and are yet to find a true successor.

Nuno Espirito Santo is their third attempt in two seasons.

That they were relying on Moyes to keep them up for a third time, needing his Everton to beat Tottenham, spoke volumes.

West Ham season lowlights The six matches that left West Ham doomed August 16: Sunderland 3 West Ham 0

Newly-promoted Black Cats produce a second-half blitz for an opening day triumph. Mads Hermansen has a debut to forget. September 13: West Ham 0 Tottenham 3

Spurs ease to victory in a match that would go on to be a costly moment in West Ham’s season. Boss Graham Potter lasts just one more game at the helm before being sacked. January 3: Wolves 3 West Ham 0

Molineux side pump former boss Nuno’s men to finally grab their first Prem win of the season. West Ham fail to conjure a single shot on target during a shocking display. January 6: West Ham 1 Nottingham Forest 2

Hammers fall seven points from safety on a night of VAR controversy at London Stadium. A narrowly disallowed goal is compounded by Morgan Gibbs-White’s 88th minute penalty, leaving the East Londoners staring into the abyss. May 10: West Ham 0 Arsenal 1

Leandro Trossard fires Mikel Arteta’s title chasers into a crucial lead on 82 minutes. West Ham think they’ve levelled in stoppage time, only for a lengthy VAR check to break their hearts. May 17: Newcastle 3 West Ham 1

With relegation rivals Tottenham having finally woken up under Roberto De Zerbi, West Ham need to get something as they travel to the North East. A miserable start, bizarre tactical switches and some shockingly poor defending lead to a fatal defeat.



Declan Rice was sold for £105million to Arsenal, which was unavoidable. What could have been avoided was pouring that money down the drain on players such as Edson Alvarez.

Recruitment is what has ruined this club.

More than £400m has been spent since Rice departed, wasted by a leadership out of touch and out of their time, relying on old boys’ networks rather than smart scouting.

There have been attempts to refresh that side of the club, in predicably calamitous fashion.



Tim Steidten was appointed as technical director in the glow of their Conference League win.

Immediately the German clashed with Moyes and Steidten was not only banned from the training ground by the Scot, but also his successor, Julen Lopetegui.

The power remains with David Sullivan, the target of fan protests all season, and still the club is an erratic mess.

Even at a basic level, things do not work.



Where do Tottenham go from here? By Dan King ON A blindingly sunny day, Tottenham Hotspur avoided a total eclipse of White Hart Lane. But never again is what they swore the time before. You remember, when they were almost relegated last year. Now they must show they actually mean it. There is no Europa League trophy to paper over the cracks. No Champions League place to keep the tills ringing. No reason for self-congratulation and pats on the back. Spurs have seen more false dawns in recent years than The Truman Show. And like the title character of that film, too many people at the club have been living in a fantasy world. It is time to face reality, and get serious. At least Tottenham now seem to have a serious manager. Roberto De Zerbi not only Dezerbs every penny of whatever survival bonus he negotiated. The Italian has also earned the kind of support and authority which has been denied to so many of his predecessors. Chelsea chiefs have seen the error of their ways and given new boss Xabi Alonso the title of manager. Even if De Zerbi remains “head coach”, he must be given a bigger say in transfers and the whole culture of the club, as Alonso has been promised. The former Brighton boss, who craved similar power at the Amex, could hardly do a worse job than those currently in charge at Tottenham. The club is apparently searching for a second sporting director to work along Johan Lange, the not-so-great Dane who cannot hide behind injuries to avoid a massive share of the blame for the current situation. Former Tottenham defender Jan Vertonghen, who was studying to become a football executive even before his retirement, has issued the equivalent of a come-and-get-me plea. Spurs could do a lot worse than the Belgian who was part of the Mauricio Pochettino teams which twice challenged for the Premier League title and reached the final of the Champions League only seven years ago. Vertonghen knows what the club is about and what the standards were. He, or someone else in a senior role in the footballing department, needs to restore them. But in the end, it always comes down to players. A fish rots from the head down, and Cristian Romero should not be the captain of a dinghy, let alone a Premier League football club. The Argentinian has let Spurs down too often, on and off the field. Romero must be sold, even if it is at a loss. So should fellow centre back Micky van de Ven, if he is not committed to the cause. Any sales would add to the kitty to buy the reinforcements De Zerbi requires to start moulding the team in his image. But some things, like leadership, are priceless. Which is why signing Liverpool legend Andy Robertson and Bournemouth defender Marcos Senesi on free transfers makes so much sense. Young Spurs players like Lucas Bergvall and Archie Gray, who have known little but turmoil as the club lurched leaderless towards the brink, need strong characters around them to set the tone. There is the core of a good team here. But everyone at Tottenham said that last year, too. It is time for action, not words. For daring and for doing.

Some areas of the stadium ran out of beer. Hammers fans could not even cry into a pint.

Money has been thrown at problems time after time, to little success.

Deals are left late in a bid to cut the cost, but players are constantly and damagingly overpaid for.

So much so that the club’s accounts warned this year of a serious shortage of cash come this summer, whether they stayed up or not.



A more than £100m firesale is needed before the Championship season begins and the club will have to swallow the fact that they will not be getting the prices they want for their players.

It was ironic that, ahead of the Leeds, game Jarrod Bowen featured in an advert for a 50 per cent sale.

There have been brief moments this year when it looked like, against all odds, West Ham would survive.

But Nuno took too long to settle on a starting XI, messing about early on with Andy Irving – another calamitous signing – in midfield, passing up precious points.

Regardless of those decisions by the Portuguese boss, blame for this circus lies solely in the boardroom, at the feet of Sullivan and all who have stood by him.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sullivan did not even remain in his seat in the directors’ box until the final whistle, making his escape early before any potential protest from supporters.

Sports.title: Premier League’s final European spots CONFIRMED as Chelsea miss out after disastrous last-day defeat at Sunderland
Sports.content:
THE Premier League’s European places have been decided after a tense final day of sweating and swapping.

After a finale with SIX teams competing for spots across the Champions League, Europa League, and Conference League, EIGHT sides will be preparing for action on the Continent next season.





And that could still rise to nine if Crystal Palace win the Conference League in midweek and take the back door into the Europa League.

Sunderland were the day’s big winners, going above Chelsea with a 2-1 win at the Stadium of Light.

Regis le Bris’ promoted men qualified for the Europa League barely 12 months after coming up from the Championship.

They knew a victory would be enough to secure a place in the Conference League at least, but were helped out by Brighton losing to Manchester United on the South Coast.

READ MORE ON FOOTBALL TOP OF THE SLOTS Best bet365 slots: Top 20 games for UK players in 2026

Their players watched on nervously in a huddle for the full-time whistle as Brentford drew with Liverpool.

Celebrations erupted when their seventh-place finish was confirmed.

Xabi Alonso will not be in Europe next season at Stamford Bridge, though, as Chelsea tossed away their chance of making anything of another dismal campaign.

Despite results going their way – Brighton losing at Manchester United – they put in another shambolic performance and lost to Sunderland, who simply wanted it more and showed all the quality of a side heading towards history.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Blues have spent over £1.7billion under owners Clearlake Capital and Todd Boehly only to finish outside of the European places twice in four years.

Their Prem finishes since the 2022 takeover are 12th, sixth, fourth, and tenth.

Liverpool, meanwhile, clung on to fifth and cemented their position in the Champions League again on a day of goodbyes in front of the Kop – regardless of whether Arne Slot will be there to oversee it moving forward.

They had to avoid an unlikely scenario of defeat at Anfield and Bournemouth, beating Forest to edge their way into the top five.



Elsewhere, Bournemouth could only draw at Forest, but even a win would have made no difference in their hopes of reaching the Champions League as Aston Villa came from behind to beat Manchester City.

The Cherries still had themselves a Europa League place guaranteed but needed Villa to finish fifth and therefore make sixth into a Champions League one and go even better.

Brentford, who looked in control of a Europa League spot heading into May, threw it away somewhat and couldn’t take advantage of other results, meaning they did not get into any of the three competitions.

Brighton fans and players were watching on in hope like Sunderland after a 3-0 defeat to United, and will go into the Conference League.

A point for them would have had them above Sunderland, but that was never looking likely at the Amex.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool star calls for Arne Slot sack after latest reality check - 'It's horrendous'
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool star calls for Arne Slot sack after latest reality check - 'It's horrendous'

Liverpool rounded out their underwhelming season with a draw against Brentford at Anfield as Arne Slot's position is called into question by a former player

View 2 Images Arne Slot has seen his Liverpool future questioned this term

Former Liverpool star Jermaine Pennant claimed the Reds' draw with Brentford on the final day should be "the nail in the coffin" for Arne Slot as he ripped into their latest below-par performance.

‌



The Merseysiders were champions this time last year, winning with ease in the Dutchman's debut year. But he's endured a steep decline in his second season despite being backed to the tune of over £400million last summer.

‌



Liverpool's season has been somewhat hampered by injuries to key players, but the performances levels and glaringly obvious issues haven't been addressed and have plagued Slot's side all season.

‌



A fast start to the season quickly tailed off and Slot faced questions over his future. Liverpool could only draw with Brentford on the final day, which saw them finish fifth, and Pennant insists the hierarchy have to wake up and make the difficult decision.

Mohamed Salah left in floods of tears as legendary Liverpool career comes to an end READ MORE :

How much every Premier League team has earned this season as final positions confirmed READ MORE :

He said on social media: "The board can not be sitting in the directors box watching this absolute garbage, and think and talk amongst themselves, and come to the conclusion that this manager will be challenging for silverware next season!!! Hanging on to Brentford. This should be the nail in the coffin."

He went on to add: "FSG please READ this….. Against the top 9 teams, home and away is 18 games. Liverpool have won 3……. Yes I said 3…… just do the right thing for the club and these players!!!! Because your eyes see and watch exactly what we ALL see. And it’s horrendous."

‌



The draw with Brentford came after the damaging defeat at Aston Villa nine days ago. The Reds were beaten 4-2, adding a consolation in added time, but the performance showcased the issues that have existed in Slot's side for much of the season.

View 2 Images The Reds have endured several difficult moments this season

Slot has recently claimed he expects to remain in his role for next season. Xabi Alonso, who was seen as a likely candidate to replace him if Liverpool did opt for a change, is no longer on the market having taken the Chelsea job.

‌



The Dutchman will seek to transition the side, which he had attempted this season with the club signing a different profile on player to what they were used to under Jurgen Klopp. Mohamed Salah will be a high profile departure, albeit he has become a less influential figure this term.

Slot is under pressure to make the signings of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz work at Anfield given their sizeable fees.

Sports.title: Sky Sports forced to apologise after Pep Guardiola's tear-jerking Man City goodbye speech
Sports.content:
Sky Sports forced to apologise after Pep Guardiola's tear-jerking Man City goodbye speech

Pep Guardiola spoke emotionally on the Etihad Stadium pitch when addressing the Manchester City supporters after his final match as their manager after a decade in charge of the club

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola delivered an emotional speech on the Etihad Stadium pitch after his final match in charge of Manchester City (Image: Sky Sports)

Sky Sports were forced to apologise after Pep Guardiola dropped an f-bomb in his Manchester City goodbye speech. Guardiola was visibly emotional when speaking for the final time as City manager on the Etihad Stadium pitch.

‌



The Catalan coach choked back his tears and could barely speak at first when addressing the club's supporters on Sunday evening. He ended the speech by declaring “it has been f****** fun” which prompted an immediately apology to viewers from the Sky match commentator.

‌



Guardiola paid tribute to his family during the speech, especially his 94-year-old father, Valenti, who travelled over for the occasion. He also spoke about the honour of having a statue built and the North Stand now bearing his name.

‌



Erling Haaland fumes at VAR as Pep Guardiola's Man City goodbye ends in defeat READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola breaks down in tears as Man City players form guard of honour READ MORE :

A tribute video also played over screens inside the stadium. Guardiola referred to it multiple times while on the microphone.

He said: "A minute of silence, please. I am so nervous, terrified. Why do you love me so much? Why do you do that to me?

"I never... [Ten more years chants, Pep shakes his head]. No, just for Erling (Haaland). I never could have imagined the amount of love. It is a tremendous honour to be your manager. I would love to not just remember the trophies. Hopefully, we provide you with these unbelievable feelings and emotions that people who come here feel they have fun.

‌



View 2 Images Pep Guardiola's father, Valenti, who turned 95 years old on Saturday, was at the Etihad Stadium to watch his son's final match in charge of Manchester City (Image: Sky Sports)

"Let me have a little break, my dad is here - 95 years old. Maybe he doesn't realise, but I am pretty sure Cris and my dad realise that there is a stand which is really beautiful and my family is there for many years.

‌



"Thank you, Sheikh Mansour, but I am sure Khaldoon put real pressure on. My family, they will be here.

"The players do not know it, but I will be there controlling them to make legacies. Fernandinho, Eddy, John, Bernie, all the players on the screen. The players have a huge responsibility to continue the standards of this amazing club.

"From day one, it is my home. In the next years, and you find me in the streets, if you are a City fan, come to me and hug me. I mean it.

"Like I said it has been a huge honour to represent this club. Every decision I thought what was best for this club. I love you so much. Let me finish what I said a few days ago, they didn't allow me to say it, but it has been f****** fun."

Sports.title: Premier League LIVE: West Ham RELEGATED, Spurs safe and European places confirmed
Sports.content:
The final day of the Premier League is here

The 2025/26 Premier League season is over, with West Ham joining Burnley and Wolves in the Championship next season, while Liverpool have sealed Champions League football

West Ham United have been RELEGATED from the Premier League despite a 3-0 win against Leeds United. Nuno Espirito Santo's side needed to beat the Whites and hope Everton would do them a favour at Tottenham.

However, even though West Ham were convincing winners at home to Leeds with Jarrod Bowen among the goalscorers, Tottenham won 1-0 against Everton to seal Premier League survival, sending the Hammers down to the Championship following a 14-year stint in the top flight.

Elsewhere, Liverpool have sealed their place in the Champions League next season after a nervy 1-1 draw against Brentford at Anfield. They end the season in fifth, with Bournemouth sixth and booking a spot in the Europa League after Andoni Iraola's side were held to a 1-1 draw at Nottingham Forest.

Joining them in the Europa League are Sunderland, who have finished seventh after a huge 2-1 win at home to Chelsea, who themselves have ended up in 10th and without European football next season. Brighton are the final Premier League side to have qualified for Europa via the league, with the Seagulls in the Conference League.

Aston Villa went to Manchester City and won 2-1, Manchester United were 3-0 winners at Brighton, Burnley and Wolves played out a 1-1 draw, Arsenal earned a 2-1 victory at Crystal Palace, while Fulham beat Newcastle United 2-0 in the other Premier League matches on Sunday afternoon.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland fumes at VAR as Pep Guardiola's Man City goodbye ends in defeat
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland fumes at VAR as Pep Guardiola's Man City goodbye ends in defeat

Manchester City ended their campaign with a 2-1 defeat by Aston Villa, as Pep Guardiola's farewell didn't get the desired result, and Erling Haaland was left fuming at the officials

View 3 Images Phil Foden was adjudged to be offside

Erling Haaland didn't hold back in his assessment of VAR after Manchester City were denied a late equaliser in Pep Guardiola's final match. City ended their campaign with a 2-1 defeat by Aston Villa after Phil Foden's late goal was chalked off.

‌



Antoine Semenyo gave a much-changed City side the lead before an Ollie Watkins brace turned the game on its head. Guardiola, John Stones and Bernardo Silva were all saying goodbye to City, who failed to find an equaliser to end the season with a loss.

‌



Watkins' winner was initially ruled out for offside before the VAR deemed that Ruben Dias had played the England striker on. And VAR was to rule in favour of Villa once more later on.

‌



Foden smashed in via the underside of the crossbar to make it 2-2 in the last minute, only for his goal to be ruled out. The VAR graphic showed just how tight the decision was and, after Guardiola slumped back into his seat disappointed, Haaland picked up his phone to post on Instagram.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Pep Guardiola breaks down in tears as Man City players form guard of honour READ MORE :

How much every Premier League team has earned this season as final positions confirmed READ MORE :

With nothing to play for and City assured of second place, the Norwegian goal machine was given the day off. But he didn't take a day off from sharing his opinion.

‌



"Hmmm not sure," Haaland wrote as a caption to the offside call with a crying laughing emoji.

The Premier League match centre wrote on X: "VAR checked the referee’s call of goal – and established that Foden was in an offside position and recommended that the goal was disallowed."

There were tears for Silva, who was given a guard of honour after being substituted off, Stones, who also received an ovation, and for Guardiola, who ends a decade in charge of the club. The Catalan leaves having won 20 major trophies.

‌



3 View 3 Images He wasn't happy with the call (Image: Instagram/@erling) 3 View 3 Images Erling Haaland was on a watching brief (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Given the microphone on the pitch after the final whistle, Silva said: "It's really tough to put into words my feeling toward man city, towards you guys, because I don't think I will ever feel the same about another team in my life.

‌



"The love I got from this club, from you guys, I doubt I will get it again. So thank you so much. All the memories we have together, with my brothers, with you, the staff, this is a family. It will forever be my family and I am really grateful."

Stones said: "I can't express my gratitude enough. To feel the love you have all given me over these 10 years, it's been a dream come true. From the bottom of my heart, thank you so much. It's been an honour to wear this shirt, to play for this club, it's been an absolute privilege.

"This will always be my home. I look forward to watching the games with out all in the stands. From the bottom of my heart thank you so much for all the memories. I hope we made everyone's dreams come true."

But on the pitch at least, it was victory for Villa and goals for Watkins, who heads to the World Cup in good form. The result secured fourth place for Villa, who won the Europa League in mid-week to secure a first trophy for 30 years.

Sports.title: Arsenal finally get their hands on Premier League trophy after Crystal Palace win
Sports.content:
Arsenal finally get their hands on Premier League trophy after Crystal Palace win

CRYSTAL PALACE 1-2 ARSENAL: A much-changed Gunners side finish their title-winning campaign with a win as both sides turn their attention to upcoming European finals

View 3 Images Arsenal lift the Premier League title at Selhurst Park

After a gruelling 22-year wait for Premier League glory, the sweltering conditions were never going to halt Arsenal's title party.

‌



As chants of "we are unbearable," boomed out from a jubilant and celebratory sea of red inside a shaded corner of Selhurst Park, the heavily-rotated Gunners did what they have done for most of the season before finally getting their hands on the trophy they have long hunted.

‌



There is just no getting away from the fact this was a game both teams could have done without, particularly as the scorching temperatures did not represent ideal preparation for major European finals.

‌



Arsenal looked like they'd blown a 2-0 lead late in the day when Yeremy Pino thought he'd snatched Crystal Palace a late point, however, the Spanish substitute's strike deflected off Evann Guessand, who was standing in an offside position. Even if the goal would have stood, you can't say it would have mattered a great deal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Premier League's European teams confirmed as Champions League and Europa League spots secured READ MORE :

West Ham relegated from Premier League and braced for fire sale as Tottenham secure safety READ MORE :

Six days out from the Gunners' heavyweight Champions League showdown with PSG in Budapest, Arteta unsurprisingly made nine changes but it underlines Arsenal's strength in depth that they were still able to see the job through courtesy of goals from Gabriel Jesus and Noni Madueke.

‌



There was also still time for Max Dowman to write himself into the history books once again. He went clubbing with the Arsenal squad in Mayfair on Tuesday evening following their crowning moment, missed Champions League final media day on Thursday due to his GCSE examinations before becoming the youngest ever player to start a Premier League match at just 16 years and 144 days.

Meanwhile, Oliver Glasner also shuffled his pack yet still received a worrying injury blow just over 72 hours out from their Conference League final clash with Rayo Vallecano in Leipzig. Adam Wharton started on the bench, came on at half-time and hurt his ankle in a challenge with Myles Lewis-Skelly, who like his fellow countryman, also missed out on Thomas Tuchel's England World Cup squad this week.

View 3 Images Adam Wharton went off injured (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

‌



Wharton attempted to soldier on but was unable to continue and Glasner's face told its own story. He left the field unassisted and headed back to the dressing room for treatment. Despite the absence of Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze from Arsenal's starting XI, they certainly did not struggle to create opportunities.

First Jesus curled an effort against the post inside the opening four minutes before Noni Madueke drove the rebound straight at Dean Henderson. Jesus then raced through and fluffed an attempt to dink Henderson when he instead should have squared to compatriot Gabriel Martinelli.

Then it was Martinelli's turn to squander a glorious opportunity before he turned provider for Jesus' opener. The Brazilian, who netted twice at Selhurst Park last season, now has more final-day Premier League goal involvements (six goals, two assists) than any other player in the entire division.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal continued the party at Selhurst Park (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Palace pulled one back through Jean-Philippe Mateta's header which denied Arsenal the chance to match a club-record 30 wins without conceding - set by Bertie Mee's legendary Double-winning side of 1971 - in all competitions before Guessand's late effort was chalked off.

Before Arsenal's ecstatic players headed back inside to change into their home strip, there was some concern over Piero Hincapie, who was seen clutching his ankle at the full-time whistle.

Sports.title: Tottenham survived but this is still their most embarrassing day in the Premier League
Sports.content:
Tottenham survived but this is still their most embarrassing day in the Premier League

Tottenham Hotspur secured their survival on the final day of the Premier League season with a 1-0 win over Everton as Joao Palhinha scored the only goal of the game

View 3 Images Roberto De Zerbi celebrates' Spurs' triumph (Image: Will Cooper/Shutterstock)

There should be no cause for celebration. You can understand the huge overwhelming sense of relief in the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium at the final whistle.

‌



The stadium began to chant “We are staying up” after Roberto De Zerbi did his best David Pleat impression as the Spurs boss ran onto the pitch with echoes of Luton’s great escape at Manchester City all those years ago. The players then went round the pitch to whip up the fans to celebrate with the long-suffering fans as if it was some sort of miraculous great escape from relegation.

‌



And when they began to play “Glory, Glory Tottenham Hotspur” it showed that this great club has truly forgotten what it stands for. Maybe you can indulge the fans this time - but rival supporters will be looking on to see how far this great club has fallen.

‌



No-one should remember this day as anything other than the lowest, most embarrassing point for Tottenham in the Premier League era.

It has been an utter shambles on the pitch, off the pitch and this must serve as a warning to the club’s hierarchy this can never be allowed to happen again.

West Ham relegated from Premier League and braced for fire sale as Tottenham secure safety READ MORE :

You have to credit the Tottenham fans because they were so loud before kick-off and they created a remarkable atmosphere to lift and inspire the players.

‌



Incredibly, this was Tottenham’s first home win in the Premier League in this calendar year, a run which stretches back 170 days to December 6 when they beat Brentford 2-0 under Thomas Frank’s reign.

They have had two managers since then and, after Igor Tudor’s disastrous caretaker spell, De Zerbi has finally managed to lift this group of underperforming players to safety.

Ultimately, Joao Palhinha scored the goal to secure the win, Spurs’ safety and yet really far too many of them should hang their heads in shame.

‌



View 3 Images Joao Palhinha celebrates after his goal proved Spurs' winner vs Everton (Image: 2026 Shutterstock Editorial. )

This is no one-off freak of a season. They finished fourth from bottom last season and have finished 17th again. This whole club needs a reset.

Six years ago, they had pretensions of being part of the European Super League and, from there, they have become perennial strugglers who have survived by their skin of their teeth. Again. They built their magnificent 60,000 stadium to become one of the biggest clubs in Europe and yet so nearly dropped into the Championship. They were lucky West Ham were even worse.

‌



Frankly, they were also very lucky they faced an Everton side who looked like they were already on the beach and had two players - Jordan Pickford and James Garner - papped coming out of a strip club this week.

There was never really a sense of jeopardy in the stadium because it was always going to take Tottenham to lose, West Ham to win and Spurs never went behind. The news filtered into the stadium that West Ham were ahead and you could sense the nerves and tension. When the board went up to show nine minutes of added time, there were huge groans

However, Tottenham have been so bad this season they still thought one Everton goal might change all that. That is how bad Spurs have been. The fans feared they could still lose it.

‌



Spurs keeper Antonin Kinsky made a sensational save from Everton substitute Tyrique George deep into injury time. Kinsky, the fall guy in the Champions League at Atletico Madrid, made another incredible stop to deny Leeds victory two weeks ago. He did similar at Wolves.

View 3 Images Randal Kolo Muani of Tottenham Hotspur and Roberto De Zerbi (Image: 2026 Shutterstock Editorial)

Those are the small margins which have Tottenham in the top flight. Last season, Tottenham at least won the Europa League. But they still did not learn their lesson.

‌



If they do not improve this summer then they only have themselves to blame. De Zerbi looks to have the energy and hunger needed.

But when the TV cameras panned to the directors’ box during the game, you could see the nerves etched over the faces of the hierarchy. No wonder.

It would have been a disaster on every level and one of the biggest stories in the history of the Premier League if they had gone down. It cannot happen again.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah left in floods of tears as legendary Liverpool career comes to an end
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah left in floods of tears as legendary Liverpool career comes to an end

Mohamed Salah made his final appearance for Liverpool on the Premier League's final day and was overcome by emotion as he bid farewell to Anfield and Reds supporters

View 2 Images Mo Salah broke down in tears following his final Liverpool appearance (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool star Mohamed Salah broke down after his final appearance for the club. The Egyptian forward made his last outing for the Reds on the final day of the Premier League season on Sunday.

‌



Arne Slot's men drew 1-1 with Brentford to secure a spot in the Champions League. Salah was taken off midway through the second half at Anfield and appeared to keep his emotions in check as he walked off the pitch.

‌



But it was a different matter after the game as Salah walked around the Anfield pitch one final time. He clearly had tears in his eyes as he bid farewell, before receiving a gift from club chiefs Billy Hogan, Richard Hughes and club icons Kenny Dalglish and Ian Rush.

‌



Salah has yet to confirm what his plans are next, but sent a clear message to his now former teammates in a training ground speech the day before the Brentford game.

“Wait, one more thing I want to say,” the Egyptian forward said. "Being Liverpool, to win something for Liverpool and win games, it’s the best thing that could happen to you.

Andy Robertson pens emotional open letter to Liverpool fans ahead of final game READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



“I think it’s the best club in the world when you win something – and the worst club in the world when you lose. So you better win next year!”

Salah moved to Liverpool in 2017 following some impressive exploits in Italy, where he'd impressed with Fiorentina and Roma. Prior to that he had been a squad player at Chelsea and deemed surplus to requirements, but he quickly made a mockery of that status.

In his debut year the Egyptian would scoop the PFA Player of the Year award - one of three he would win during his time in England. He would also break the record for goals scored in a Premier League season, a record since taken by Erling Haaland.

‌



View 2 Images Salah leaves Anfield after a glittering career (Image: Getty Images)

Salah was part of the Liverpool side that ended their wait for top flight glory, proving crucial in the 2020 triumph. He was again central when they won it again last year. His first major honour was the Champions League in 2019, where he would score the opener in the final.

The forward will leave Anfield as the club's third highest scorer of all-time. Only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt sit above him in the list with Salah sitting ahead of icons like Steven Gerrard, Robbie Fowler and Kenny Dalglish.

Article continues below

Salah will depart Liverpool a year ahead of schedule having signed a two-year deal towards the end of last season, but the decision has been made to part ways 12 months early after a disappointing season for the 33-year-old.

Sports.title: Mo Salah enjoys classy Liverpool farewell but moment with Arne Slot tells its own story
Sports.content:
Mo Salah enjoys classy Liverpool farewell but moment with Arne Slot tells its own story

Liverpool ended their season with a 1-1 draw against Brentford at Anfield as club legends Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah said goodbye with their final appearances for the Reds

View 4 Images Mohamed Salah of Liverpool applauds the fans as he is substituted off at Anfield for the final time (Image: 2026 Gaspafotos/MB Media)

No doubt there are some old-school, hard-bitten football followers who are not overly impressed by guards of honour.

‌



Never mind guards of honour that are actually staged DURING a match.

‌



But you would have to be a particularly cold fish to be disapproving of the sight of team-mates forming a tunnel of appreciation and celebration for Mohamed Salah as he left the pitch for the last time as a Liverpool player. It was a poignant, beautiful moment, followed by a tearful Salah kissing the Anfield turf goodbye.

‌



It was then followed by the most cursory of hand-clasps with Arne Slot and a token, one-sided hug - but that is another story.

And you wait years and years for a mid-game guard of honour and then another comes along straight after it! The second one, of course, was for Andy Robertson. Those moments were just the precursor for the wonderful sign-offs that followed after the final whistle.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Andy Robertson pens emotional open letter to Liverpool fans ahead of final game READ MORE :

Michael Owen fires warning to Arne Slot and tells him what needs to happen at Liverpool READ MORE :

Salah would have wanted to finish with a goal but had to make do with an assist and a very good individual performance.

It would probably be a touch harsh to suggest the search for a storybook farewell had Salah as motivated as he had looked all season. But only probably.

There was certainly plenty of vintage Salah, that is for sure. And amidst the emotion of the occasion, a significant footballing matter was evident.

‌



Salah is leaving a year before his contract was due to expire. And does Salah have a year of Premier League effectiveness left in his legs? Absolutely he does. And probably then some.

He has not been at his best and most effective this season but he remains an elite talent. A club other than Liverpool its going to get the benefit of that talent.

View 4 Images Mohamed Salah, in tears, hugs team-mate Virgil van Dijk in his final appearance for Liverpool

‌



View 4 Images Andy Robertson says farewell to Anfield for the final time

Although Milos Kerkez has belatedly looked up to the left-back job, the same is almost certainly true of Robertson. If these two club stalwarts initiated their departures, then there is no issue. But their absence next season will be keenly felt by Liverpool.

Salah was a constant threat to a Brentford side that struggled to get any sort of early foothold in the game.

‌



How Keith Andrews’ side lasted for almost an hour without conceding was down to some poor Liverpool decision-making. But that has been the story of their season. But this contest was slightly unusual in that the main theme quickly became a case of whether or not Salah could sign off with something special.

And Salah duly obliged. He looked a fraction offside before providing a lovely assist for Curtis Jones but VAR got into the spirit of things and allowed the goal to stand.

It was the 120th assist of Salah’s 442-game Liverpool career. It was his 93rd assist for Liverpool in the Premier League, taking him to the top of that chart, ahead of Steven Gerrard.

‌



View 4 Images Two men going their separate ways this summer (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

And it was one that actually shook Brentford into action. They did, after all, have something to play for and a win would have taken them into a European spot.

But after Kevin Schade’s headed equaliser, neither side could find a winner - Dango Outtara missed an added-time sitter - and the stage was left for Robertson and Salah - by now making no attempt to fight back the tears - to take the stadium’s acclaim for one final time.

Article continues below

It is fair to say they got the send-off their magnificent Liverpool careers demanded.

Sports.title: Why Arsenal are worthy Premier League champions
Sports.content:
A moment of joy. Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard got his hands on the Premier League trophy and lifted it in scenes that will define a generation and an era for the football club.

All season, fans, pundits, analysts and experts have put in their tuppence about Mikel Arteta's side this season.

Their style of play has been branded "unwatchable", they have been given the tag 'Set-Piece FC' - yet none of that matters when you get your hands on the trophy.

Arsenal have faced their so-called critics despite being consistently top of the table since October.

Earlier this year, Paul Scholes said they would be the "worst Premier League title winners ever". The notion that Arsenal do not have a clear enough 'Premier League Player of the Season' winner has been used as a stick to bash the Gunners with.

It follows criticism throughout the season about their style - the comments made by Fabian Hurzeler about Arsenal's time-wasting in March appearing to be the height of those complaints. Arteta sarcastically responded: "What a surprise" - a sign he was getting fed up of the criticism of his team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikel Arteta reacts to Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler's comments on his team 'time-wasting' during their Premier League victory

Even in the days since their title win was confirmed, there have been plenty of comments on social media about how 'VARsenal' won the title due to fortunate refereeing decisions.

It included Liverpool head coach Arne Slot having a thinly-veiled dig at Arteta's Arsenal this week. "Congratulations to them," he said. "But for me they have been a different champion to the last 10 seasons. It is the first time in 30 years that 40 per cent of goals had come from set-pieces."

None of that will matter to Arteta, his players and staff - nor the Arsenal supporters whose title celebrations will carry on all summer.

Yes, they did not always show the attacking verve of Manchester City, or have the crucial goalscorer at the top of the Golden Boot rankings. But they did enough in front of goal to win the league - especially when criticism about their style of play has not totally been their own fault.

All season, opposition teams have gone - or dropped - to huge lengths to stop Arsenal getting their way in the final third.

The numbers help show how guarded opposition teams have been against Arsenal. This season, Arsenal have taken the most open-play shots in the Premier League where the opposition has nine or more players in the penalty box at the time.

Datawrapper Datawrapper , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Datawrapper cookies or to allow those cookies just once.
